svg.title: Plan capacity for a host failure
svg.desc: Hypothetical capacity illustration with four equal partitions per host, not a hardware support claim. Before failure, Host A runs A1 and A2 and has two spare partitions; Host B runs B1 and B2 and has two spare partitions. After Host A fails, Host B runs all four workloads and has no GPU reserve. Compatible hardware, drivers, licensing, CPU, and memory are also required. Restart and migration eligibility must be validated; the example does not promise seamless failover or live migration.
svg.text: Plan capacity for a host failure
Read panel 1, then panel 2. Compare capacity, not migration behavior.
Example only: four equal partitions is a hypothetical supported configuration.

g.text: Each host has four equal partitions: two used and two spare.
GPU reserve across the two hosts: 4 partitions.
Host B now runs A1, A2, B1, and B2: all four partitions are used.

svg.text: Matching supported GPU hardware/drivers, valid licensing, and CPU/memory are also required.
Restart and migration eligibility must be validated for the exact configuration.
This capacity example does not promise seamless failover or live migration.
There is no remaining GPU reserve after the failure.
